title: Which Values Appear Twice
statement:
`numbers` has `n` whole numbers, and every number is between `1` and `n`. Each value appears **once or twice**.

Return the values that appear **twice**, in increasing order. Try to use only a constant amount of extra memory besides the answer.
constraints: every value appears at most twice

hints.nudge: Every value is a valid position in the list. Could you use the list itself to remember which values you have already seen?
hints.pattern: Mark visited values by flipping the SIGN of the number at index value - 1; meeting a number whose slot is already negative means a repeat.
hints.pseudocode:
result = empty
for x in numbers:
  i = |x| - 1
  if numbers[i] < 0: add |x| to result
  else: numbers[i] = -numbers[i]
sort the result and return it
hints.walkthrough: A set of seen values works in O(n) extra memory. To avoid it, notice that value v can be remembered at position v - 1 (it exists because 1 <= v <= n). When you read a number x, look at position |x| - 1: if the number stored there is positive, this is the first time you see x, so make it negative to mark 'seen'; if it is already negative, x was seen before, so x appears twice. Use the absolute value when you read, since earlier steps may have flipped signs. Collect the repeated values and sort them for the answer. Work on a copy if the original must stay unchanged. O(n) time, O(1) extra memory besides the answer.
